rules.quote: Follow the full title with the short title in parentheses
rules.specification: Apply this introduction format when a short title is used. Do not infer a requirement to invent or supply a short title for every treaty mention: the general-publication examples include a treaty identified by its title alone. Either a missing full title or missing parentheses can breach the introduction format.
rules.violation_condition: A treaty short title is introduced without the full title immediately preceding it and without the short title being enclosed in parentheses.
when: Applies when introducing a short title for use in the text.
A short title already introduced and used in the text may appear without its full title in a citation note.
rules.why: The rule-grain test separates short-title introduction format from later title choice; the title-only examples limit the interpretation.

rules.specification: The template is title, parenthesised place and date of making, square-bracketed entry-into-force year, series and applicable series or volume number, then page number. The ATS examples omit pages, so interpret the page-number component as applicable to series citations that use page references, rather than mandatory for every series.
rules.violation_condition: A detailed treaty citation omits an applicable component, gives its components in the wrong order, or lacks the prescribed parentheses around making information or square brackets around the entry-into-force year.
when: Applies when providing a detailed treaty citation in text, notes or a reference list.
In general publications, citing the treaty title alone is usually sufficient.
A short title already introduced and used in the text may replace the full title in a citation note.
Page numbers are required where applicable to the series; the supplied ATS examples omit them.
rules.why: The component list defines one citation template; G-2 and G-3 retain its scope and short-title permission as conditions.

rules.quote: Don’t use any punctuation between the elements.
rules.specification: The primary elements are the title, making information, entry-into-force year, series/number and page reference. Required brackets belong to their elements. Punctuation within making information, separators between multiple series references and a citation’s final full stop are not prohibited by this rule.
rules.violation_condition: Extra punctuation separates the primary elements of a detailed treaty citation.
when: Applies to detailed treaty citations.
Does not prohibit the required parentheses or square brackets.
Does not prohibit punctuation within an element or between multiple series references, as shown in the examples.
rules.why: The rule-grain test separates added inter-element punctuation from missing or misordered citation components; the examples constrain the prohibition.
